clue.text: Bitter nob reported a total loss

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the two words are heard rather than read

parts.note: bitter can mean wry (twisted, sour), and a nob is a toff, an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A sour aristocrat has been in the news after some disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A nob or toff is British slang for a posh, upper-class person. WRY TOFF said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged beyond repair, such as a car after a crash, is accounted a complete loss by insurers.

clue.text: Recycle waste, not wanting fine

indicators.note: not wanting means doing without, so one letter is dropped from the word for waste

parts.note: waste is refuse, rubbish
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An instruction to recycle rubbish, perhaps to avoid a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle something is to put it to use again rather than throw it away.

clue.text: Tiny parachutes let his pilot finally drift to the ground

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of pilot
drift suggests letters wandering out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: going to the ground is going down

explanation.surface: A pilot ejects and floats earthwards under a small parachute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drift' rearranges LETHIS plus T (the last letter of 'pilot') into THISTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fluffy seed heads of a thistle carry seeds through the air like miniature parachutes.

clue.text: Individual backing opera company's extremely honest at heart

indicators.note: backing in a down clue means the letters of the opera company run in reverse

parts.note: ENO is English National Opera
extremely means too, as in too kind

indicators.note: at heart points to the central letters of honest

explanation.surface: An opera company is praised for being thoroughly honest underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is only a link. English National Opera is the London opera company usually abbreviated in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial given personally to a single student is individual teaching, with nobody else involved.

clue.text: Old film buff has chat about New York Times crossword answer

indicators.note: about here means alongside, setting the chat next to the two short pieces that precede it

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fan
times as in multiplication, two by three
gas is informal for chat
a light is a word entered in a crossword grid

explanation.surface: A movie fan discusses an answer in the New York Times puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link and 'about' is used loosely for 'next to'. The newspaper name in the surface splits into a place and a multiplication word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a 1944 Gainsborough melodrama set in Victorian London, a British film now decades old.

clue.text: Grinning, gutted cracking river carp

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the outside letters go inside the river

parts.note: the Nile is the African river

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the first and last letters of grinning

explanation.surface: An angler grins at a gutted carp caught in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like the fish but is the verb meaning to complain. GG from 'Grinning' goes into NILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain pettily, and so is to quibble or find fault in small ways.

clue.text: Hunter needs gun to follow game

indicators.note: to follow means the gun comes after the game

parts.note: nim is a game of taking objects from piles
rod is American slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A hunter needs a firearm when chasing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the mighty hunter of the Bible, so his name is used for any keen huntsman.

clue.text: Begin to work on mounting

indicators.note: mounting means going up, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: Starting work on a mount, as a rider or a picture framer might.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: When a plan or team starts to function properly, it is said to come together and set.

clue.text: Young woman entertains boss, heading off weariness

indicators.note: entertains means holds within, so the shortened boss sits inside the young woman

parts.note: lassie is Scots for a girl

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob

explanation.surface: A young woman entertains her boss before he heads off, tired out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a manager but means a decorative stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is a state of physical or mental tiredness and lack of energy.

clue.text: Maiden's wee mouse

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
wee is informal for urine

explanation.surface: A girl's tiny mouse, with 'wee' as Scots for small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' reads as small but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Murine means relating to mice; mouse is used here attributively, as in mouse studies.

clue.text: Northern English lass moved house after vacation, more anon

indicators.note: moved house means relocated, so the letters are put in a new order
vacation means emptying out, leaving only the outer letters of more

explanation.surface: A northern English girl moves house after the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptying, giving ME from 'more'. 'moved house' rearranges E + LASS + ME into AMELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, describing a work whose author is unknown and uncredited.

clue.text: Fast or mostly slow?

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: lento is the musical direction meaning slowly

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is quick or slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quick, but it is the season of abstinence before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians traditionally abstain from food or luxuries for the forty days before Easter, a period of fasting.

clue.text: Oscar axes stupid description of "original copies"?

definitions.note: this definition is a phrase describing a self-contradictory expression, and the answer is the adjective for one

parts.note: O is Oscar in the radio alphabet
the x and y axes of a graph
moronic means stupid

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner cuts something foolish from a description of film copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like a verb but is the plural of axis.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase like 'original copies' combines contradictory terms, making it a figure of self-contradiction.

clue.text: Blob of ordure is dreadfully strong-smelling

parts.note: a blob is a round shape, so the letter O

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lump of dung gives off a terrible smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' rearranges O + OF + ORDURE + IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Odoriferous means giving off a smell, usually a strong or unpleasant one.

clue.text: Millions should stop only bracketing Newton with gravity

indicators.note: should stop means plugging a gap, so the letters for millions and Newton go inside together
bracketing means enclosing, so the word for only holds the inserted letters

parts.note: solely means only
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A physics lesson about Newton and gravity, with some big numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gravity' suggests Newton's physics but means seriousness; 'should stop' and 'bracketing' both describe the same insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something solemnly is to do it seriously and with dignity, in a grave manner.

clue.text: Worker needs old key, but I'm off

indicators.note: off means taken away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: imperative means essential, key
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker needs an old key, but someone is leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a lock but means crucial.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a factory hand or machine operator, someone doing practical work.

clue.text: Leader ditched extra responsibility

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is thrown away

parts.note: a bonus is something extra

explanation.surface: A boss who quit took on extra duties.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty that falls on someone.

clue.text: Plump former soldiers eat before light entertainment

indicators.note: eat means take inside, so the plump and soldiers pieces enclose the word for before

parts.note: to plump for is to opt
ere is an old word for before
TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force renamed the Army Reserve

explanation.surface: Overweight ex-servicemen eat early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' reads as fat but is the verb, plump for. The Territorial Army is now called the Army Reserve, so it is 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short, light opera with spoken dialogue, an easy-going kind of show.

clue.text: Somewhat inhumane Roman?

indicators.note: somewhat means part of, so the answer lies within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A question about a rather cruel Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the emperor was notoriously cruel, so calling him somewhat inhumane is an understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor Nero was infamous for cruelty, including the persecution of Christians.

clue.text: A paper lies regularly — its boss is given notice

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of paper lies is taken

parts.note: a newspaper's boss is its editor, ED

explanation.surface: A newspaper keeps printing lies, and its editor is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given notice' suggests dismissal but means informed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be apprised of something is to be told or informed about it.

clue.text: Appear happy about one figure of speech

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for appearing happy wraps the numeral

parts.note: to smile is to look happy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone appears pleased with one turn of phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile compares one thing to another using like or as, a standard rhetorical device.

clue.text: Could be a pill largely like Nurofen, for a start? Right

definitions.text: Could be a pill largely like Nurofen, for a start? Right

indicators.note: could be means the letters might become something else, so they are rearranged
largely means most of the word, so the last letter of pill goes
for a start means the first letter of Nurofen

explanation.surface: Suggesting something is a tablet rather like a branded painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges A + PIL + LIKE + N + R. The whole clue also describes the answer. Nurofen is a British brand of ibuprofen.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic tablet such as ibuprofen is taken to relieve aches, so a branded pill fits.

clue.text: So I must repress resistance

indicators.note: repress means hold down within, so the self contains the letter

parts.note: the ego is the I, the self
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A determination to hold back one's urge to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' looks like a link but is the definition, meaning therefore.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used to introduce a conclusion.

clue.text: Returning airman takes one inside for dance

indicators.note: returning means going back, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
takes means the airman is joined to the next piece

parts.note: PO is a pilot officer in the RAF
someone inside is a prisoner, an old lag

explanation.surface: A homecoming pilot brings someone indoors for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: An old lag is British slang for a convict. 'Returning' turns POLAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: The galop is a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance in quick duple time.

clue.text: Trivial Pursuit initially provided brief period of fun

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of pursuit

parts.note: if means provided that
a fling is a short spell of enjoyment

explanation.surface: A game of Trivial Pursuit offers a short burst of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Trivial Pursuit is the quiz board game, but 'Trivial' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffling means unimportant or paltry, too small to matter.

clue.text: Brewer's volume omits family tree

indicators.note: omits means leaves out, so the family word is removed

parts.note: a firkin is a brewer's cask measure of nine gallons
kin means family

explanation.surface: An edition of Brewer's reference book leaves out the family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewer's volume' suggests Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable but means a measure of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fir is an evergreen conifer, a familiar kind of tree.

clue.text: Love to let rip? Drive slowly

indicators.note: to let rip is to go wild, so the letters are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: love is zero, O in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Someone loves to let loose, yet prefers to drive gently.
explanation.definitionFit: To tootle is to go along in a leisurely way, typically in a car.

clue.text: Start of self-addressed letter? How sad!

definitions.meaning: a letter written to oneself would open with a greeting to oneself
an exclamation of mild dismay or sympathy

explanation.surface: Someone writes themself a letter, and it is rather pathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned exclamation of regret, and also the salutation of a note addressed to oneself.

clue.text: Part of church school expels one spoilt pest

indicators.note: expels means throws out, so the numeral is removed

parts.note: to school is to train
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: spoilt means damaged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church school expels a spoilt troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun but is the verb, train. 'spoilt' rearranges PEST into SEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the arm crossing the nave of a cross-shaped church building.
